solve.method: T-2850: re-solved by tools/glessner_north_pairs.py with the north gable pairs' sill and head left free (solved, principal point free). Fixed controls: 8; pair corners at plan W: 16. The pairs read sill 19.77 ft, head 24.61 ft.
solve.limitations: Hand-picked aperture edges partly obscured by poles; plan spacings +/-0.4ft. This camera is a photographic fit, not a surveyed exposure station. The north stack crest and the tower depth control are model-derived off-plane controls (residuals 15.33 and 14.68 px); the east eave reads 23.68 px. The free principal point is weakly constrained. Not a whole-view exact match.
solve.light: T-2848, read off the photograph: the north gable and tower are a silhouette against a bright sky, with glare up and to the right of the gable (south-south-west, behind the house), the poles in front are backlit, and nothing on the north face throws a shadow. So the sun stands behind the building and the face the camera sees is lit only by the sky. Azimuth about 200 degrees is read from the glare; the elevation (40 degrees) is not readable here and is set so the north face falls in shade, which is the reading.
solve.picks_note: T-2850: aperture_controls_W_z_px are T-2470's picks. Their z column is the height T-2470 assumed (20.0 / 25.25 ft); T-2850's solve uses only each pick's W and row and solves the pair's sill and head.
